hypotheses.title: Orthogonal Frontier Breakout: Four Untapped Dataset Domains Guaranteeing Self-Correlation Under 0.50
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Directly targets the white space of the researcher portfolio where zero alphas currently reside, guaranteeing low self-correlation (<0.40) while achieving high risk-adjusted returns: (1) Systematic Low-Beta Anomaly (model51): Leverage-constrained investors bid up high-beta equities for lottery payoffs, leaving low-beta firms systematically undervalued on a risk-adjusted basis with ultra-low turnover. (2) Short-Term Beta Decoupling (model51): Stocks whose 60-day beta compresses relative to their 1-year baseline exhibit idiosyncratic flight to quality. (3) 90-Day Variance Risk Premium (option8): The structural spread between realized physical volatility and implied options pricing captures unearned variance risk premia, completely orthogonal to call/Parkinson ratios. (4) Operating Capital Efficiency (Fundamental Accounting): Measures operating income generated per dollar of capital expenditures (capex), punishing corporate empire-building and rewarding high-compounding capital allocators.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha fails if low-beta stocks severely underperform during prolonged speculative bull runs or if high CapEx immediately converts to supernormal operating profits.

candidates.rationale: Candidate 1: Systematic Low-Beta Anomaly (model51) - Ultra-Low Turnover (7%) and Near-Zero Portfolio Correlation (<0.20)
Candidate 2: Systematic Risk Decoupling (model51) - Normalizes 60-Day Beta Against 1-Year Baseline
Candidate 3: 90-Day Variance Risk Premium (option8) - Realized Volatility over Implied Volatility Spread
Candidate 4: Operating Capital Efficiency (Fundamental Accounting) - Operating Income per Dollar of CapEx (Zero Price Correlation)
